newsitem.title: CHINA: HK handover is dream for China stamp lovers.
newsitem.headline: HK handover is dream for China stamp lovers.

text.p: Hong Kong's return to China at midnight on Monday is a collector's dream for thousands of philatelists in the Chinese border city of Shenzhen, a city stamp official said.

More than 6,000 people were expected to queue for a midnight frank on a golden commemorative stamp bearing the face of late leader Deng Xiaoping, who negotiated the British colony's return to China, against the Hong Kong skyline, the manager of the city's new stamp exchange, Li Sen, said on Sunday.
The stamp had a face value of 50 yuan ($6.0), but the price had already more than doubled to 120 yuan, said Li, general manager of the Shenzhen City Jintuo Stamp Centre and Interchange.
The market would issue 6,000 of the stamps from midnight, with one allowed to each person who had already registered, he said. Orders had poured in for two months, he said.
With all the stamps sold in advance, the rush would be to get a frank as close as possible to midnight, the moment Hong Kong's 156 years of British colonial ended, he said.
"It's the hottest stamp in China, although anything with a Hong Kong handover theme is hot now," he said.
The Jintuo market opened its doors to local collectors on June 21, but would officially open at midnight on Monday to frank the commemorative stamp, Li said.
Such is the popularity of stamp collecting in China that people have queued at the market's doors from 5.00 a.m. -- or three hours before formal opening hours, he said.
More than 100 stalls were leased to stamp traders and total daily turnover since June 21 had topped 100 million yuan, Li said.

The array of Hong Kong handover memorabilia includes postcards franked in Hong Kong showing Deng chatting with former British Prime Minister Margaret Thatcher in 1984, commemorative Hong Kong telephone cards with a face value of HK$100 ($12.8) but selling at up to 350 yuan ($42), and HK$25 ($3.0) subway passes for 100 yuan ($12).
